text:
Lena (Security): Heads up — discovered several public repos with hardcoded API keys. We should update the in-app banner and revoke flow copy. Current banner: 'Exposed API key detected' feels too terse.
Priya (Design): Agree. It reads like an error code. Need plain language, action-first. Maybe 'We found an exposed API key — rotate it now to protect your data.'
Sam (Product): Action-first is good. Also want to clarify whether keys are auto-rotated. Our current behavior: we don't auto-rotate; we block keys only if "flagged" by abuse system. Need to be explicit.
Lena (Security): Correct. We mark keys as "flagged" and we can revoke them manually. We should encourage rotation and link to docs.
Diego (Frontend): For the banner CTA, should we show 'Rotate key' (primary) + 'View details' (secondary)? 'Rotate' triggers modal.
Priya (Design): Wording options for banner body: 1) 'We found an exposed API key in a public location. Rotate the key now to prevent unauthorized access.' 2) 'An API key associated with this project appears public. Rotate it to secure your project.' Prefers 1 for urgency.
Marta (Accessibility): A few a11y notes: 1) Banner should not rely solely on color (red) to convey severity — include icon + text 'High risk'. 2) Ensure the 'Rotate key' button has accessible name that includes key name if possible.
Sam (Product): Modal copy needs to say what rotation does: 'Rotating will create a new key and immediately disable the old key. Any running services using the old key will stop working.' We should also mention rollback path: 'You can re-create keys but old key remains disabled.'
Priya (Design): Modal structure suggestion: Title = 'Rotate API key', Body = 'Rotate now to issue a new key and immediately disable the old one. Update any apps using this key.' Helper line (muted): 'This will invalidate the current key immediately. You will need to update any deployed integrations.' CTA = 'Rotate key' (destructive style? It's a security action but not destructive to data). Secondary = 'Cancel'.
Lena (Security): Add a checkbox 'Also revoke old key' by default unchecked? Wait rotation implies disabling old key. Maybe keep toggle 'Notify team via email' default on.
Diego (Frontend): UX constraint: rotation is synchronous and we show a toast: 'Key rotated — new key copied to clipboard (show/hide)'. We need safe copy behavior: don't auto-copy to clipboard without user confirmation; show the new key in a masked field with a copy button.
Marta (Accessibility): The masked key must be reachable by screen readers and offer 'Show key' button. If we show the key, it should be in a dialog with aria-modal and focus trap. Use aria-describedby to include helper text about secure storage.
Priya (Design): Microcopy for the modal confirmation checkbox: 'I understand that rotating will invalidate the current key.' That forces awareness. Consider making it required for non-admins? Product decision.
Sam (Product): We should not force checkbox for org admins, but require it for maintainers in orgs with >10 projects. Implementation detail for later. For copy, use: 'I understand that rotating this key will immediately disable the existing key.'
Lena (Security): Suggest adding a small inline link 'How rotation works' that opens docs explaining revocation, audit logs, and recommended update patterns.
Diego (Frontend): Banner behavior question: Do we show banner only to owners/admins or everyone with key access? Probably owners + maintainers. Who sees it determines CTA wording: if a viewer cannot rotate, CTA should be 'Request rotation' instead.
Priya (Design): Good point. Copy vary by role: Owner/Maintainer = 'Rotate key'; Viewer = 'Request rotation' with a tooltip 'This action sends a request to admins.'
Marta (Accessibility): Also ensure banner has role='status' and is keyboard focusable for screen reader users to notice it.
notif-bot: Audit: security.exposure.detected event created for project=alpha, key_id=key_abc123, actor=lena, ts=1714009999.
Sam (Product): Error state copy if rotation fails: 'Rotation failed. Your existing key is still active. Try again or contact support.' Small retry CTA 'Try again'.
Priya (Design): For the toast after rotation: 'API key rotated. Remember to update your integrations.' with an 'Copy key' button. Keep toast persistent until dismissed for 10s. Also include 'View instructions' link.
Marta (Accessibility): Toast must be aria-live='assertive' when rotation completes. If we include the key in the toast, be very careful with screen reader verbosity. Better to put key in a focused modal after rotation so SR users can access securely.
Diego (Frontend): I'll implement: role-based banner variants, rotate modal with masked key and copy button, required confirmation checkbox for certain roles, toast + docs link.
Lena (Security): Copy final suggestion for banner: Title: 'Exposed API key found' Body: 'We found an API key for this project in a public location. Rotate the key now to prevent unauthorized use.' Primary CTA: 'Rotate key' Secondary: 'View details' Helper: 'This action will invalidate the current key immediately.'
Priya (Design): I like that. Tiny tweak: change title to 'Publicly exposed API key' (reads a bit clearer).
Sam (Product): Decision: use Priya's title + Lena's body. Role-based CTA text as discussed. Action items below.
Diego (Frontend): ACTION: PR with banner variants + rotate modal + a11y hooks by EOW.
Priya (Design): ACTION: Update Figma components and provide copy tokens.
Marta (Accessibility): ACTION: Add SR test for focus, aria-live, and masked key flow.
Lena (Security): ACTION: Draft docs blurb for 'How rotation works' and recommended steps.
Sam (Product): I'll coordinate translations for the banner strings.
Priya (Design): I'll drop final strings in the PR description. :sparkles:
Diego (Frontend): Quick question — should the banner include an inline severity pill like '[High risk]'? It might be redundant.
Marta (Accessibility): If you include a pill, ensure it's programmatically readable and not only a color cue.
Priya (Design): Let's include a small 'High risk' label visually and for SRs.
Sam (Product): Great work, team. We'll monitor feedback and iterate if users find rotation confusing.
